citation: (1) Raman, N., Cao, M., Tsvetkov, Y., Kästner, C., Vasilescu, B. 'Stress and Burnout in Open Source: Toward Finding, Understanding, and Mitigating Unhealthy Interactions'. ICSE 2020 NIER, 8 July 2020. https://2020.icse-conferences.org/details/icse-2020-New-Ideas-and-Emerging-Results/13/Stress-and-Burnout-in-Open-Source-Toward-Finding-Understanding-and-Mitigating-Unhe ; preprint https://cmustrudel.github.io/papers/raman20toxicity.pdf. (2) Tidelift, '2023 state of the open source maintainer report' (survey fielded late 2022); summary post by Chris Grams, 25 May 2023: https://dev.to/tidelift/maintainer-burnout-is-real-almost-60-of-maintainers-have-quit-or-considered-quitting-maintaining-one-of-their-projects-51ma
source_tier: (1) Peer-reviewed short paper (NIER track, emerging results). (2) Company research (Tidelift survey) reported via Tidelift's own blog post.
access_status: (1) Preprint PDF fully read as text; ICSE abstract page read. (2) Tidelift blog summary read; the full report PDF was NOT opened (only search snippets saw its 2023 report listing). [uncertain] for report-level detail such as exact n.
sponsor_and_incentive: (1) Academic (CMU, UMD); no sponsor checked in the text I read. (2) Tidelift sells paid maintainer and open source supply-chain services, so it has an incentive to stress maintainer strain.
exact_quotes: Raman et al. abstract page: "Toxic conversations may demotivate and burn out developers, creating challenges for sustaining open source." Preprint: "toxic issues are rare, with about 6 for every 1 000 issues." Preprint: "Our best classifier had a precision of 0.91 and a recall of 0.42." Preprint: "the classifier achieved 50 % precision on the random issues." Preprint: "the rate of toxic issue discussions is substantially lower for corporate projects (statistically significant, Wilcoxon p < .001)." Tidelift post: "Fifty-eight percent of maintainers have either quit (22%) or considered quitting (36%) their maintenance work on a project"; "just under half (44%) said they were experiencing burnout."; "Hundreds of maintainers responded."; "In late 2022, Tidelift fielded its second survey of open source maintainers." (Quotes via WebFetch extraction; the Tidelift ones should be re-checked character by character against the live page.) [uncertain]
date_and_recency: Raman et al.: presented July 2020; issue data covers 2012-2018. Tidelift: survey late 2022, post May 2023. A 2024 Tidelift survey exists (reported ~60% quit or considered quitting) but I did not open it.
key_claims: Raman et al.: toxic conversations may demotivate and burn out developers; they build an SVM toxicity classifier for GitHub issues; toxicity is rare, varies by community, lower in corporate projects, and fell 2012-2018. The paper frames burnout as motivation and research agenda, not a measured outcome. Tidelift: most maintainers have quit or thought of quitting; 44% reported burnout.
headline_figures: Tidelift 2023 (survey late 2022): 58% quit (22%) or considered quitting (36%) maintaining a project; 43% had not; 54% cite other life/work priorities; 51% lost interest; 44% 'experiencing burnout'. Raman: ~6 toxic issues per 1,000; classifier precision 0.91, recall 0.42 on validation; 50% precision on 100 hand-checked random-sample predictions; 1,732,124 issues classified in the longitudinal study. 22%+36% = 58% checks arithmetically.
sample_unit_and_population: Raman: GitHub issues from GHTorrent (not people), open source projects generally. Tidelift: open source maintainers who responded to Tidelift's survey, 'hundreds' (exact n not found; I did not open the full report). Self-selected respondents. Not specific to professional software teams.
observed_vs_stated: Raman: observed text (issue comments), no burnout measured. Tidelift: self-reported.
what_it_measures_or_defines: Raman: no burnout measure; toxicity in issue text is the proxy for a stressor. Tidelift: the 44% burnout figure is a self-report; the definition/question wording was not seen in the blog post. [uncertain]
mechanism_or_cause: Raman: frequent demands for features and fixes, sometimes aggressive in tone, from users (abstract per ICSE page; also preprint intro). Tidelift: quitting reasons were other priorities (54%) and lost interest (51%); burnout is one of several.
interventions_and_effects: Raman: none tested; proposes automated detection and future mitigation. Tidelift blog: no tested interventions with effect sizes found in what I read; maintainer pay and support are the company's pitch.
transfer_to_software_teams: Weak. Open source maintainers are often unpaid volunteers facing users, unlike employed teams. Useful as an analogy for demand pressure and tone, not as an employee burnout rate.
limitations_stated: Raman is a NIER paper calling itself a 'first step'. Classifier recall is only 0.42 and precision fell to 50% on random issues, so counts are noisy; authors say 'Some noise is acceptable for studying toxicity trends in the wild'. Tidelift limitations not seen. [uncertain]
counter_evidence: Raman finds toxicity declining 2012-2018 and rare (~0.6% of issues), which cuts against a simple rising-toxicity story. Tidelift's 44% is a self-selected, vendor-run survey. The 22%+36% quitting figure is not burnout.
verification_status: Raman claims: checked in opened preprint and ICSE page. Tidelift 58/22/36/44 figures: checked via Tidelift's own blog summary opened by fetch, not the full report; secondary search snippets agree on 58/22/36. 44% burnout seen only in the blog fetch. [uncertain] for 44% wording. Did not verify any Linux Foundation or GitHub burnout figure; dropped.
usable_claim: In Tidelift's 2023 maintainer survey (fielded late 2022), 58% of respondents said they had quit or considered quitting maintaining a project, and Tidelift reports 44% said they were experiencing burnout. Raman et al. (2020) argue toxic issue conversations can burn out developers but did not measure burnout; they found toxic issues rare and declining 2012-2018.
do_not_use: Do not say Raman et al. found or measured burnout rates. Do not equate 58% with burnout. Do not use Linux Foundation or GitHub figures (unverified). Do not use the 2024 Tidelift ~60% figure (not opened). Do not present 44% as representative of all developers.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the three named essays' text; no check was made. [uncertain]
